provenance: 30 new AI-authored training examples with author-assigned labels. Not human-certified or real OCR. Each concept's examples are conservatively linked to its existing augmentation student group for selection. No human challenge text is copied. Designed after v1 error analysis; not evaluation data.

examples.label: present
examples.text: Put mashed banana extract in a tube and add Benedict reagent. Warm this mixture in a hot water bath. The heated tube may form a green, orange or brick red precipitate indicating reducing sugar. A blue result after the same treatment is negative.

examples.label: partial
examples.text: Add blue Benedict reagent to a little diluted honey in a tube. A yellow or brick red precipitate is evidence of reducing sugar. The practical steps written here stop after mixing; there is no heating instruction.

Biuret test instructions: add sodium hydroxide and copper sulphate to the sample. A violet colour indicates protein. Milk contains protein as well as other substances.

examples.label: present
examples.text: At fixed temperature, current in an ohmic resistor is directly proportional to the potential difference. V/I is constant and equals resistance, so V = IR. If R = 12 ohms and I = 0.5 A, V = 6 V.

examples.label: partial
examples.text: For Ohm's law use V = IR. The resistance is found by dividing voltage by current. At fixed temperature the current is inversely proportional to voltage; a stronger voltage therefore gives less current in this same resistor.

examples.label: missing
examples.text: A circuit needs a complete path for charge flow. Closing the switch completes the path through the bulb. An open switch makes a break. Draw the battery and lamp symbols with connecting wires.

examples.label: present
examples.text: Lithium-6 and lithium-7 each have three protons. They have different neutron numbers: three and four. Such atoms are isotopes, with the same atomic number and different mass numbers. Changing neutron count does not change the element.

examples.label: partial
examples.text: Two isotopes of lithium have the same atomic number and different mass numbers. The heavier one supposedly contains an extra electron. Both have three neutrons according to this drawing. The extra electrons cause the mass difference.

examples.label: missing
examples.text: The electrons of a neutral aluminium atom occupy shells in the arrangement 2,8,3. Losing three electrons produces a positive ion. There are still thirteen protons in the nucleus after this electron transfer.

examples.label: present
examples.text: Sexual reproduction forms a zygote by fusion of male and female gametes. Genetic information comes through both gametes. Asexual reproduction has one parent and no gamete fusion; the offspring are usually genetically identical. Dividing bacteria illustrate the asexual mode.

examples.label: partial
examples.text: Asexual reproduction has one parent and occurs without fusion of gametes. Offspring are usually genetically identical to that parent. Strawberry runners give new plants using this method. The notes explain only this reproductive mode.

examples.label: missing
examples.text: A germinating bean grows a root and a shoot. It needs oxygen, moisture and suitable warmth. Stored food supplies energy before new leaves can support the growing plant. In the experiment the dry seeds did not germinate.

examples.label: present
examples.text: Combination makes one product from several reactants. Decomposition breaks a compound into simpler substances. Single displacement replaces one element of a compound with another element. Double displacement exchanges ions between two compounds. These four descriptions classify the changes in the reactions.

examples.label: partial
examples.text: Single displacement replaces an element in a compound with another element. An iron nail can displace copper from copper sulphate solution. Double displacement exchanges partners between two compounds, often forming a precipitate. This page covers displacement only.

examples.label: missing
examples.text: During an experiment record the initial and final colour, any bubbles and any temperature change. Smell gases only by the instructed safe technique. A physical observation is different from the conclusion drawn from it. Wear eye protection.

examples.label: present
examples.text: During inspiration the diaphragm contracts and flattens and the ribs move up and out. The larger chest cavity volume lowers the pressure below outside air pressure, drawing air in. In expiration muscles relax, ribs move down and in and the diaphragm becomes dome shaped. Chest volume gets smaller, pressure rises above outside pressure and air goes out.

examples.label: partial
examples.text: For inspiration, the diaphragm contracts and flattens. Intercostal muscles lift the ribs up and out. Chest cavity volume increases and pressure drops below atmospheric pressure, so air enters the lungs. There is no description here of the outward phase.

examples.label: missing
examples.text: The trachea divides into two bronchi. Smaller bronchioles end in tiny alveoli. Cartilage helps keep the larger airway open. Mucus traps some dust and cilia move it towards the throat.

examples.label: present
examples.text: Doping adds a small controlled impurity amount to silicon to increase conductivity. Pentavalent donor atoms give an extra electron: electrons are the majority carriers in n-type silicon. Trivalent acceptors such as boron leave holes: holes are the majority carriers in p-type silicon.

examples.label: partial
examples.text: Doping is adding a small controlled amount of impurity to silicon. Boron is a trivalent acceptor; its three outer electrons leave an electron vacancy called a hole. Holes are majority carriers in p-type material. The explanation here covers only the acceptor case.

examples.label: missing
examples.text: An intrinsic semiconductor is a pure material. Heat can create electron-hole pairs by freeing bonded electrons. In pure silicon, electrons and holes are generated together in equal numbers. Cooling reduces the number of thermally available carriers.

examples.label: present
examples.text: A 0.4 kg metal piece has c = 500 J per kilogram per degree. Warming it from 15 C to 35 C gives a temperature change of 20 C. Q = mc times the change = 0.4 x 500 x 20 = 4000 joules. In insulated mixing, heat lost by the hotter object equals heat gained by the cooler object.

examples.label: partial
examples.text: Use Q = mc times the temperature change to find heating energy. The temperature change is final minus initial temperature. Mass is in kilograms when c is per kilogram per degree, and Q is in joules. This note does not explain the energy balance between two mixing bodies.

examples.label: missing
examples.text: Boiling water absorbs latent energy while its temperature remains at the boiling point at fixed pressure. Q = mL describes the energy for this change of state. For m = 0.3 kg and L = 2260000 J/kg the energy is 678000 joules. This is vaporisation, with no liquid warming step.

examples.label: present
examples.text: Put the starting dye spot on a pencil baseline above the solvent level. In paper chromatography the paper is the stationary phase and the solvent is the mobile phase. Dyes separate into bands at different distances because attraction to paper and solubility in solvent differ.

examples.label: partial
examples.text: Chromatography separates dyes as solvent moves along paper. Paper is the stationary phase and solvent is the mobile phase. Different dyes have different attraction to paper and solvent. This explanation does not describe where to place the starting sample spot relative to the liquid.

examples.label: missing
examples.text: Pour muddy water through filter paper in a funnel. Mud stays behind as residue while the filtrate passes through. Some very fine material may remain suspended. Filtration is used here to remove insoluble dirt from water.

examples.label: present
examples.text: An appliance takes 5 A at 240 V. P = VI = 240 x 5 = 1200 W = 1.2 kW. Power is the rate of energy transfer: each watt means one joule per second. A longer operating time uses more total energy even when power stays constant.

examples.label: partial
examples.text: A device takes 3 A from a 24 V supply. P = VI = 24 x 3 = 72 W. Power is energy transferred each second; the watt means one joule per second. This note gives no conversion between watts and kilowatts.

examples.label: missing
examples.text: A kettle changes electrical energy mostly into heat, while a loudspeaker produces sound. Energy can be transferred into several forms at once. Insulation can reduce wasted heat transfer to the surroundings. An energy flow diagram shows these transfers.
